expert_proposals.title: Enlarge buffer cache and align planner I/O costs to cut GetUserTweets terminal occupancy
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: shared_buffers=16384 (128MB) is tiny versus 2TB RAM, so the GetUserTweets working set is not retained; low_buffer_hit_ratio is active and DataFileRead/BufferIO waits appear. Planner costs (random_page_cost=4, seq_page_cost=1, effective_io_concurrency=1) undervalue cached random reads, reinforcing physical I/O on the dominant transaction.
expert_proposals.mechanism: GetUserTweets consumes 88.5% of finite client terminal time at p50=196us/p95=410us, so its per-call physical read cost directly caps TPS. Raising shared_buffers retains the hot tweets working set, cutting DataFileRead/BufferIO stalls. Raising effective_cache_size and effective_io_concurrency plus lowering random_page_cost/seq_page_cost makes the planner prefer cached index paths and prefetch, reducing per-call latency and terminal occupancy. This is the mandatory buffer_cache_capacity bundle, distinct from the refuted predicate-lock action.
expert_proposals.query_effect: Cached index scans on tweets replace physical DataFileRead paths for GetUserTweets; planner favors index over seq scans with lower random_page_cost.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Increase successful_transaction_tps by reducing GetUserTweets terminal occupancy.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: 4x current 128MB to 512MB, within safe range 8192-65536; ample RAM (2TB) makes this safe.
Raise to 8GB estimate, within 131072-1048576; reflects large host RAM.

Slight reduction paired with random_page_cost, within 0.5-2.0.

If the working set already fits and DataFileRead waits are incidental, buffer enlargement yields no measurable TPS change.

expert_proposals.title: Expand buffer cache and align planner I/O costs to cut physical reads
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: shared_buffers=16384 (128MB) is tiny versus 2TB RAM; blks_read_per_txn=1.51 vs blks_hit_per_txn=9.23 (~14% miss) and random_page_cost=4.0 overprices cached random reads, so GetUserTweets (88.5% terminal capacity) pays physical I/O.
expert_proposals.mechanism: GetUserTweets dominates terminal capacity (0.885) and its p50=196us is inflated by physical reads: blks_read_per_txn 1.51 against blks_hit 9.23. Raising shared_buffers to 65536 (512MB) retains the hot tweet/user working set; raising effective_cache_size to 1048576 tells the planner most reads are cached; effective_io_concurrency=8 enables prefetch; lowering random_page_cost to 1.1 and seq_page_cost to 0.9 makes index paths on cached pages cheaper. Together they should cut blks_read_per_txn and GetUserTweets latency, freeing terminal capacity for more completed transactions.
expert_proposals.query_effect: Index scans on tweet/user tables should hit shared_buffers instead of disk; planner prefers index paths on cached pages, reducing GetUserTweets p50 and p95.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Increase successful_transaction_tps by reducing GetUserTweets terminal occupancy.
expert_proposals.expected_latency_effect: Decrease GetUserTweets p50/p95; overall p95 modestly lower.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: 4x current 128MB to 512MB, within safe [8192,65536]; 2TB RAM leaves ample headroom.
Raise from 1 to 8 for prefetch, within safe [0,256].
Lower toward cached-read cost, within safe [1.0,6.0].
Slight decrease paired with random_page_cost, within safe [0.5,2.0].
knob_changes.mechanism_role: I/O cost scale paired with random_page_cost

predictions.rationale: Larger cache plus cache-aware planner costs reduce physical block reads.
Fewer physical reads shorten the dominant transaction's median.
Lower terminal occupancy on GetUserTweets frees capacity for completed transactions.

alternatives.statement: If buffer expansion does not move blks_read_per_txn, the residual is WAL sync latency (sync_average_ms 0.131) and the wal_commit_path bundle is the better lever.
If blks_read_per_txn falls but TPS is flat, the bottleneck is client terminal serialization rather than storage and cache tuning is exhausted.

expert_proposals.why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent leaves shared_buffers at 128MB with a 14% buffer miss and default planner costs; the mandatory buffer_cache_capacity bundle directly targets the active low_buffer_hit_ratio phenomenon and the dominant GetUserTweets transaction.

expert_proposals.title: Reverse predicate-lock direction: tighten max_pred_locks_per_page/relation
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: Prior action raised max_pred_locks_per_page 2->16 and max_pred_locks_per_relation -2->64; paired result was early_stopped_worse (-14.4% TPS, GetUserTweets p99 +25%). The direction is falsified, so reverse it with equal-or-larger safe amplitude.
expert_proposals.mechanism: The prior test increased predicate-lock granularity, which lengthened GetUserTweets p99 by 25% and cut TPS 14.4% with zero lock waits and zero retries. That refutes the 'more SIRead slots reduce promotion' direction. Reversing to a tighter-than-default granularity (page 0, relation 0) forces coarser SIRead locking, reducing per-tuple predicate-lock bookkeeping on the dominant read path. With lock_waiting_backends and conflicts at 0, the cost of coarser locks is bounded, while the benefit is less lock-table churn per GetUserTweets transaction.
expert_proposals.query_effect: GetUserTweets (88.5% of terminal capacity) should see lower p99 as predicate-lock bookkeeping per scan shrinks; no plan change expected.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Increase successful_transaction_tps versus the refuted treatment; target at least parity with the 21876 control and ideally above.
expert_proposals.expected_latency_effect: Decrease GetUserTweets p99 relative to the 1644us treatment value; bounded by zero lock waits.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Reverse of falsified 2->16; 0 is the safe low bound, forcing coarser page-level SIRead locking.
Reverse of falsified -2->64; 0 is the safe low bound, coarsening relation-level SIRead locking.

predictions.rationale: Reversing the falsified granularity increase should recover the 25% p99 regression seen in the treatment.
Recovering the -14.4% TPS loss from the refuted direction; coarser SIRead locks reduce per-txn lock churn.
Baseline lock waits are already 0; coarser locks must not introduce blocking waits.

alternatives.statement: If TPS is instead limited by WAL sync cadence, tightening predicate locks will be neutral and wal_buffers/wal_writer_delay changes would move TPS.
If low_buffer_hit_ratio drives GetUserTweets latency, shared_buffers/effective_cache_size changes would move blks_read and p99 rather than predicate-lock knobs.

cross_domain_requirements: unverified interaction note (demoted to pending constraint): shared_buffers
unverified interaction note (demoted to pending constraint): wal_buffers
expert_proposals.why_exceeds_incumbent: The prior granularity increase was falsified (early_stopped_worse). Reversing to tighter-than-default predicate-lock granularity is the only untested direction in this knob family and directly targets the dominant GetUserTweets path with zero observed lock-wait risk.
